item.title: Third weekend of protests looms as tensions persist across France
item.description: For the third Saturday in a row, people across France are set to take to the streets to protest against the high cost of living and demand better funding for education. Police are preparing for all eventualities ahead of another weekend of protests, following earlier demonstrations that ended in rioting and looting in city centres. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Meet 12-year-old Indian-American Sophia Parekh, who has given over 8,000 free books to children
item.description: Sophia Parekh, a 12-year-old from Westfield, New Jersey, has distributed more than 8,000 free books to children across the US through Sophia's Book Stand, a project she started at age seven during the Covid pandemic. She personally selects books based on children's ages and interests and also supports teachers in underserved schools. Her efforts earned her recognition as a runner-up for the 2026 Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Chinese telecoms giants in Washington’s crosshairs as FCC weighs fresh curbs
item.description: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) is proposing a ban on Chinese telecommunications companies obtaining American telephone numbers, citing national security concerns and the need to protect domestic networks. The proposed rules could prevent China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom and other service providers from obtaining numbers through internet-based voice services, the commission said on Thursday. The regulator is scheduled to vote on the proposal at its November 19 meeting.... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: France network outage puts Nokia under scrutiny as EU pushes to phase out Huawei, ZTE gear
item.description: A mobile network outage in France this week has raised questions about the reliability of Finnish telecoms giant Nokia’s products against the backdrop of continued European Union efforts to phase out Chinese suppliers Huawei Technologies and ZTE over security concerns. The problem first hit the network of France’s biggest telecoms provider Orange at 11.37am on Monday and lasted until 8.30pm, resulting in outages of up to nine hours for some customers, Orange France CEO Jerome Henique told French... item.description: Australian mushroom murderer Erin Patterson lost a bid to overturn her convictions and had a harsher sentence imposed on Friday, failing to prove she was wrongfully jailed for killing three people with a poisoned lunch. Patterson was found guilty last year of murdering her husband’s parents and elderly aunt, deliberately lacing their beef Wellington meal with highly toxic death cap mushrooms. item.title: How UKHarvest turned food waste into 10 million meals
item.description: In 2017, Yvonne Thomson founded UKHarvest to address food waste and assist individuals facing food insecurity. Initially starting with one van, the charity has impressively salvaged 10 million meals throughout its journey. Its initiatives, including Community Food Hubs and Grub Clubs, offer not only affordable food but also valuable education. Collecting about 10 tonnes of excess food weekly, UKHarvest enjoys the patronage of Queen Camilla, amplifying its community impact. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Taking antibiotics? Eating a lot of sugar at the same time may make the damage to your gut worse, scientists have found, suggesting that what you eat during a course of antibiotics could affect how well your body recovers
item.description: Research findings indicate that a diet high in sugar can significantly affect the diversity of gut bacteria in patients undergoing antibiotic therapy. The study monitored the food intake and gut microbiome of hospitalized cancer patients treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, revealing a strong connection between elevated sugar levels and shifts in gut bacteria. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: DRC Ebola clinic celebrates departure of last confirmed cases
item.description: Medical staff were joined by local residents as they celebrated the departure of the last Ebola patients from a treatment center in DR Congo’s Ituri province. item.description: Los chimpancés tienen un parentesco increíble con los humanos. Solo tenemos un 1,2% de ADN diferente. Pero entonces, ¿por qué somos aparentemente tan distintos? Es cierto que los chimpancés son animales muy inteligentes , pero no tanto como los humanos. item.title: Para tener las patatas frescas y sin brotes hay que guardarlas en la nevera y no en la despensa, según un grupo de expertos
item.description: Dentro de las cocinas españolas hay algunas tradiciones que no cambian, puesto que se han ido pasando entre generaciones. Una de estas es la necesidad de almacenar siempre las patatas en la despensa, en un lugar que sea fresco y alejado de la luz, pero que casi nunca es el frigorífico. Pero ahora hay algunas voces que nos están diciendo que meter este tubérculo en las neveras puede no tener repercusiones negativas. Un estudio. El hecho de conservar las patatas de manera diferente a lo que lo han hecho nuestras madres viene de una investigación británica que se llevó a cabo entre los años 2020… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: El misterio de las ITS en España: las infecciones de transmisión sexual dan un frenazo brusco tras años desbocadas
item.description: Las enfermedades de transmisión sexual son un problema de salud pública de primer nivel, y durante casi una década las gráficas de evolución nos mostraban cómo no paraban de aumentar año tras año con un importante incremento tras el fin de las restricciones de la pandemia. Sin embargo, los últimos datos que tenemos encima de la mesa muestran un escenario mucho más positivo con un frenazo a este incremento. El informe elaborado por el Centro Nacional de Epidemiología del Instituto de Salud Carlos III muestra una ralentización evidente en el incremento de estas infecciones. item.title: Meta y Snap llegan a juicio por acusaciones de adicción y daños a la salud mental en adolescentes
item.description: Adolescentes demandaron a Meta y Snap por presuntamente provocar problemas de salud mental y generar adicción a través de sus plataformas. El proceso comenzó este 28 de octubre en Los Ángeles y se extenderá durante varias semanas.
